newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains track sterling, end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains track sterling, end mostly down.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended mostly narrowly down, after a day spent tracking sterling's moves against other European currencies, trader said.

May, the most active contract on wheat, last traded 0.35 stg lower at 101 stg, its low for the day, having seen a high of 102.00 in earlier trading. March wheat rose by 0.50 stg, to 99.40, but only one lot of March changed hands and all other contracts ended down.
May volume was 302 of a total 633 lots.
Barley was traded unchanged, with November, the most active contract, last traded at 94.75 stg. November volume was 15 of a total 19 lots.

News of French bids for more than a million tonnes of wheat ahead of the EU tender helped the market to its highs. But by the time they got news of the award of 480,000 tonnes, traders had decided the amount was less important than it looks.
"It's not too exciting," one said, pointing out that the bids, and the award, were high because there is no EU tender next week.
"Currency's been the main factor," he said.

Sterling slid during the morning, weighed by dollar mark weakness, and then moved up against the mark, especially after comments U.S. by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan which fuelled rate hike expectations.
